summary: BLOCKED — Frontend UI testing of Partner Help & Support could NOT be performed because the backend at https://api.webhubmaster.shop rejects the current preview origin https://mobile-customer-nav.preview.emergentagent.com with 400 'Disallowed CORS origin' on ALL /api endpoints (verified via curl preflight and via browser console). Every browser fetch to /api/site/config, /api/notifications/push-config, /api/auth/send-otp, etc. is blocked by CORS. Consequently the Expo web build stays on the onboarding screen with a full-screen 'No Internet Connection' modal (the app's offline fallback triggered by failed site/config fetch), which also blocks the 'Skip' and 'Next' buttons behind it. Cannot login (neither OTP flow nor the previously-used demo-partner button — the button is not rendered because the login screen is never reached), therefore cannot navigate to /partner/support to exercise any of the acceptance items (list, filters, create ticket, thread bubbles, attach, details sheet, close, regression). Static code review of the two changed files (frontend/app/support/index.tsx, frontend/app/support/[id].tsx) shows all required testIDs are present (support-header, new-ticket, support-search, support-range, support-status, support-sort, support-empty, ticket-subject, ticket-message, submit-ticket, ticket-thread-header, ticket-details-btn, close-ticket, ticket-reply, send-reply, attach-file) and category/priority chips include 'refund' and 'urgent' respectively; message rendering uses m.at, day separators, system centered bubble, own green bubble with tick, and the details bottom sheet lists Ticket ID/Department/Priority/Status/Created/Updated/Attachments/Your other tickets — code looks parity-complete vs the described Web SupportCenter.

critical.issue: Backend CORS rejects origin https://mobile-customer-nav.preview.emergentagent.com — preflight returns HTTP 400 body 'Disallowed CORS origin'. Blocks the entire web preview; app falls back to offline screen and login is unreachable.

integration_issues.issue: Because api.webhubmaster.shop CORS blocks the preview origin, the Expo web build shows the persistent 'No Internet Connection' overlay on /onboarding/intro. Skip/Next/demo-partner cannot be reached, so Help & Support flow cannot be exercised in the browser at all.

action_items: Add https://mobile-customer-nav.preview.emergentagent.com (and any sibling *.preview.emergentagent.com used by the testing pipeline) to the CORS_ORIGINS allowlist of the api.webhubmaster.shop backend, OR point EXPO_PUBLIC_BACKEND_URL of this preview build at an in-cluster backend whose CORS is already permissive. Confirm with: curl -sI -X OPTIONS -H 'Origin: https://mobile-customer-nav.preview.emergentagent.com' -H 'Access-Control-Request-Method: POST' https://api.webhubmaster.shop/api/auth/send-otp  (must return 204/200 with access-control-allow-origin echoing the origin, not 400 'Disallowed CORS origin').

After CORS fix, re-run the Help & Support acceptance flow (login via demo-partner or OTP +919000000003 / 123456 → /partner/support → list/filter/create/open thread/reply/attach button/details sheet/close ticket → regression on /partner, /partner/jobs, /partner/wallet, /partner/profile).
critical_code_review_comments: index.tsx line 33: useQuery for /support/tickets has no error toast; a failed initial load shows only the skeleton then empty state — user gets no signal that fetch failed. Consider surfacing isError with a retry.
index.tsx line 55: date-range filter uses new Date(t.created_at) without null-guard — will produce NaN comparison if created_at missing (unlikely from backend but defensive).
[id].tsx line 56: refetchInterval 3000ms is aggressive for a support thread; consider pausing polling when tab/app is backgrounded (document.visibilityState) to reduce load.

[id].tsx line 151: 'mine' fallback (sender_role !== 'admin') can misattribute a message to the current user in shared devices/multi-user scenarios before user context loads — prefer waiting for myId before rendering bubbles or defaulting to non-mine when myId is undefined.
[id].tsx line 217: send button uses opacity 0.5 for disabled state but does not visually indicate the loading state distinct from disabled (already covered by ActivityIndicator, ok).

Both files: no explicit onError toast for the /support/meta query — if meta fails the UI silently falls back to hardcoded FALLBACK_CATS/FALLBACK_PRIOS which is fine, but the parity claim 'meta-driven' may silently regress unnoticed.

success_rate.frontend: 0% executed — blocked by CORS before any Help & Support screen could be reached

context_for_next_testing_agent: Prereq: verify CORS with `curl -i -X OPTIONS -H 'Origin: <preview-url>' -H 'Access-Control-Request-Method: POST' https://api.webhubmaster.shop/api/auth/send-otp` before starting UI flow. Login path used previously (iteration_88): goto '/', click any 'Skip' text buttons, click [data-testid=skip-notifications-button] if present, then [data-testid=demo-partner], wait 5s, then goto '/partner/support'. Key testIDs to drive: support-header, new-ticket, ticket-subject, ticket-message, submit-ticket, ticket-<id> card, ticket-thread-header, ticket-reply, send-reply, attach-file (verify present only — gallery picker not automatable), ticket-details-btn, close-ticket. Categories include 'refund'; priorities include 'urgent'. Message timestamp field on API is 'at'.
rca of the issue: Root cause: the FastAPI backend at api.webhubmaster.shop reads CORS_ORIGINS from its environment (see /app/backend/server.py `allow_origins=os.environ.get('CORS_ORIGINS','*').split(',')`). In the deployed api.webhubmaster.shop the CORS_ORIGINS env is set to a fixed allowlist that does NOT include the current preview host 'support-hub-mobile-1.preview.emergentagent.com'. Reproduction: `curl -i -X OPTIONS -H 'Origin: https://mobile-customer-nav.preview.emergentagent.com' -H 'Access-Control-Request-Method: POST' https://api.webhubmaster.shop/api/auth/send-otp` → HTTP/1.1 400 'Disallowed CORS origin'. Mitigation: append this origin (and a wildcard like https://mobile-customer-nav.preview.emergentagent.com if the ASGI middleware supports it, otherwise the exact host) to CORS_ORIGINS on the api.webhubmaster.shop deployment and restart. After that, all fetches (site/config, notifications/push-config, auth/send-otp, support/*) should succeed and the Help & Support flow can be tested end-to-end.
